Public comments vs surveys

A survey starts with a question from the brand. A public comment starts with the customer. Nobody prompted it. ReplyInPublic is the inbox for that second kind of feedback. It is not a survey tool.

By Pranav Kaja. Last updated 16 November 2026.

The difference

How a satisfaction survey differs from a comment a customer already posted in public.
QuestionSurveyPublic comment
Who starts it The brand asks a question. The customer writes first.
Was it prompted Yes. The brand requested the answer. No. Nobody prompted the comment.
What it costs to collect The survey itself, and sometimes a discount code or a similar goodie for finishing. That giveaway is a cost on top of the survey. The comment is already public. Collecting it does not require a giveaway.
Who can see the outcome The brand, inside the survey. Other people reading that post, once a person replies in the thread.
Where ReplyInPublic fits It does not run the survey. It puts the comments in one inbox so a person can decide what to answer.

Why the public side is worth answering

Public feedback is more honest, because nobody was prompted. It is already there, so the brand did not pay to collect that comment. And it is visible to everyone reading: when the brand answers, those readers see a brand that cares.

ReplyInPublic helps brands move money from satisfaction and feedback surveys to answering the feedback customers already post in public. Surveys measure satisfaction. Replies earn it.

What this page does not claim

This site does not give a number for how often people finish surveys, and it does not give a dollar cost for running one. No figure of that kind is published here. A public reply is not a research panel. It is one comment, in public, that a person can choose to answer.
